main_body: A dark grey rune stone slab with a lighter grey rounded cap at rows 7-10 and a dark body with teal rune glyphs below, outlined in near-black.
top_band: Lighter grey (#5c5a64, L=92) rows 7-10 (4 rows), a straight rectangular band with only slightly rounded top corners, no wider than the body, followed by a dark outline row 11 and the dark shaft (L=69).
evidence: The 4-row lighter band at the top is the same width as the shaft and has only chamfered corners. It reads as a flat band cap, as in the red 'column: flat band cap' of the guide, not as an elliptical or wider top plate. The contrast with the shaft is only about 23 L (92 vs 69), under the 25 L step required for a top. The rest is a flat front face with painted runes. Rule 12 fails this as a straight rectangular band cap with no visible top face.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 5 distinct colours and a median of 5 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. Its dark edge pixels are 100% neutral (near-black), so it has the sticker outline. The body is a flat dark fill with only a few teal rune pixels and no grain, stone shading or per-stone variation. That is much shallower than the Beodeul references.
